audit_status.source_base: Greek 1 Peter text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact draft reviewed for wives/husbands, inner adornment, good conscience, suffering for good, spirits in prison, baptism.

verses.restored: Likewise wives, be arranged under your own husbands, so that even if some disobey the word, they may be won without word through the conduct of wives,

familiar.text: Likewise, ye wives, be in subjection to your own husbands; that, if any obey not the word, they also may without the word be won by the conversation of the wives;

modern.text: Wives, in the same way, submit yourselves to your husbands, so that even if they refuse to believe the word, they will be won over without words by the behavior of their wives

original.text: ⸀Ὁμοίως γυναῖκες ὑποτασσόμεναι τοῖς ἰδίοις ἀνδράσιν, ἵνα ⸀καὶ εἴ τινες ἀπειθοῦσιν τῷ λόγῳ διὰ τῆς τῶν γυναικῶν ἀναστροφῆς ἄνευ λόγου κερδηθήσονται

verses.restored: observing your pure conduct in reverence.

familiar.text: While they behold your chaste conversation coupled with fear.

modern.text: when they see your pure and reverent demeanor.

original.text: ἐποπτεύσαντες τὴν ἐν φόβῳ ἁγνὴν ἀναστροφὴν ὑμῶν.

verses.restored: Let your adornment not be outward braiding of hair and wearing of gold or putting on garments,

familiar.text: Whose adorning let it not be that outward adorning of plaiting the hair, and of wearing of gold, or of putting on of apparel;

modern.text: Your beauty should not come from outward adornment, such as braided hair or gold jewelry or fine clothes,

original.text: ὧν ἔστω οὐχ ὁ ἔξωθεν ἐμπλοκῆς τριχῶν καὶ περιθέσεως χρυσίων ἢ ἐνδύσεως ἱματίων κόσμος,

verses.restored: but the hidden human of the heart, in the incorruptible of gentle and quiet spirit, which is very precious before the Divine.

familiar.text: But let it be the hidden man of the heart, in that which is not corruptible, even the ornament of a meek and quiet spirit, which is in the sight of God of great price.

modern.text: but from the inner disposition of your heart, the unfading beauty of a gentle and quiet spirit, which is precious in God’s sight.

original.text: ἀλλʼ ὁ κρυπτὸς τῆς καρδίας ἄνθρωπος ἐν τῷ ἀφθάρτῳ τοῦ ⸂πραέως καὶ ἡσυχίου⸃ πνεύματος, ὅ ἐστιν ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ πολυτελές.

verses.restored: For so once also the holy women hoping in the Divine adorned themselves, being arranged under their own husbands,

familiar.text: For after this manner in the old time the holy women also, who trusted in God, adorned themselves, being in subjection unto their own husbands:

modern.text: For this is how the holy women of the past adorned themselves. They put their hope in God and were submissive to their husbands,

original.text: οὕτως γάρ ποτε καὶ αἱ ἅγιαι γυναῖκες αἱ ἐλπίζουσαι ⸀εἰς θεὸν ἐκόσμουν ἑαυτάς, ὑποτασσόμεναι τοῖς ἰδίοις ἀνδράσιν,

verses.restored: as Sarah obeyed Abraham, calling him lord; whose children you became, doing good and not fearing any terror.

familiar.text: Even as Sara obeyed Abraham, calling him lord: whose daughters ye are, as long as ye do well, and are not afraid with any amazement.

modern.text: just as Sarah obeyed Abraham and called him lord. And you are her children if you do what is right and refuse to give way to fear.

original.text: ὡς Σάρρα ⸀ὑπήκουσεν τῷ Ἀβραάμ, κύριον αὐτὸν καλοῦσα· ἧς ἐγενήθητε τέκνα ἀγαθοποιοῦσαι καὶ μὴ φοβούμεναι μηδεμίαν πτόησιν.

verses.restored: Husbands likewise, living together according to knowledge, giving honor to the feminine as weaker vessel, as also co-heirs of grace of life, so that your prayers may not be hindered.

familiar.text: Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel, and as being heirs together of the grace of life; that your prayers be not hindered.

modern.text: Husbands, in the same way, treat your wives with consideration as a delicate vessel, and with honor as fellow heirs of the gracious gift of life, so that your prayers will not be hindered. Turning from Evil

original.text: Οἱ ἄνδρες ὁμοίως συνοικοῦντες κατὰ γνῶσιν, ὡς ἀσθενεστέρῳ σκεύει τῷ γυναικείῳ ἀπονέμοντες τιμήν, ὡς καὶ ⸀συγκληρονόμοις χάριτος ζωῆς, εἰς τὸ μὴ ἐγκόπτεσθαι τὰς προσευχὰς ὑμῶν.

verses.restored: Finally, all be of one mind, sympathetic, sibling-loving, tenderhearted, humble-minded,

familiar.text: Finally, be ye all of one mind, having compassion one of another, love as brethren, be pitiful, be courteous:

modern.text: Finally, all of you, be like-minded and sympathetic, love as brothers, be tenderhearted and humble.

original.text: Τὸ δὲ τέλος πάντες ὁμόφρονες, συμπαθεῖς, φιλάδελφοι, εὔσπλαγχνοι, ⸀ταπεινόφρονες,

verses.restored: not repaying harm for harm or reviling for reviling, but instead blessing, because into this you were called, so that you may inherit blessing.

familiar.text: Not rendering evil for evil, or railing for railing: but contrariwise blessing; knowing that ye are thereunto called, that ye should inherit a blessing.

modern.text: Do not repay evil with evil or insult with insult, but with blessing, because to this you were called so that you may inherit a blessing.

original.text: μὴ ἀποδιδόντες κακὸν ἀντὶ κακοῦ ἢ λοιδορίαν ἀντὶ λοιδορίας τοὐναντίον δὲ ⸀εὐλογοῦντες, ὅτι εἰς τοῦτο ἐκλήθητε ἵνα εὐλογίαν κληρονομήσητε.

verses.restored: For the one willing to love life and see good days, let one stop the tongue from harm and lips from speaking deceit,

familiar.text: For he that will love life, and see good days, let him refrain his tongue from evil, and his lips that they speak no guile:

modern.text: For, “Whoever would love life and see good days must keep his tongue from evil and his lips from deceitful speech.

original.text: ὁ γὰρ θέλων ζωὴν ἀγαπᾶν καὶ ἰδεῖν ἡμέρας ἀγαθὰς παυσάτω τὴν ⸀γλῶσσαν ἀπὸ κακοῦ καὶ ⸀χείλη τοῦ μὴ λαλῆσαι δόλον,

verses.restored: let one turn away from harm and do good; let one seek peace and pursue it.

familiar.text: Let him eschew evil, and do good; let him seek peace, and ensue it.

modern.text: He must turn from evil and do good; he must seek peace and pursue it.

original.text: ἐκκλινάτω ⸀δὲ ἀπὸ κακοῦ καὶ ποιησάτω ἀγαθόν, ζητησάτω εἰρήνην καὶ διωξάτω αὐτήν·

verses.restored: Because eyes of Lord are upon righteous/just ones and his ears toward their prayer, but face of Lord is against those doing harm.

familiar.text: For the eyes of the Lord are over the righteous, and his ears are open unto their prayers: but the face of the Lord is against them that do evil.

modern.text: For the eyes of the Lord are on the righteous, and His ears are inclined to their prayer. But the face of the Lord is against those who do evil.”

original.text: ὅτι ὀφθαλμοὶ κυρίου ἐπὶ δικαίους καὶ ὦτα αὐτοῦ εἰς δέησιν αὐτῶν, πρόσωπον δὲ κυρίου ἐπὶ ποιοῦντας κακά.

verses.restored: And who is the one harming you if you become zealous for the good?

familiar.text: And who is he that will harm you, if ye be followers of that which is good?

modern.text: Who can harm you if you are zealous for what is good? Suffering for Righteousness

original.text: Καὶ τίς ὁ κακώσων ὑμᾶς ἐὰν τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ ⸀ζηλωταὶ γένησθε;

verses.restored: But even if you should suffer because of righteousness/justice, blessed are you. Do not fear their fear, nor be troubled.

familiar.text: But and if ye suffer for righteousness’ sake, happy are ye: and be not afraid of their terror, neither be troubled;

modern.text: But even if you should suffer for what is right, you are blessed. “Do not fear what they fear; do not be shaken.”

original.text: ἀλλʼ εἰ καὶ πάσχοιτε διὰ δικαιοσύνην, μακάριοι. τὸν δὲ φόβον αὐτῶν μὴ φοβηθῆτε μηδὲ ταραχθῆτε,

verses.restored: But set apart Messiah as Lord in your hearts, always ready for defense to everyone asking you a word concerning the hope in you, yet with gentleness and reverence,

familiar.text: But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts: and be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear:

modern.text: But in your hearts sanctify Christ as Lord. Always be prepared to give a defense to everyone who asks you the reason for the hope that is in you. But respond with gentleness and respect,

original.text: κύριον δὲ τὸν ⸀Χριστὸν ἁγιάσατε ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν, ⸀ἕτοιμοι ἀεὶ πρὸς ἀπολογίαν παντὶ τῷ αἰτοῦντι ὑμᾶς λόγον περὶ τῆς ἐν ὑμῖν ἐλπίδος,

verses.restored: having a good conscience, so that in what you are spoken against, those reviling your beautiful conduct in Messiah may be put to shame.

familiar.text: Having a good conscience; that, whereas they speak evil of you, as of evildoers, they may be ashamed that falsely accuse your good conversation in Christ.

modern.text: keeping a clear conscience, so that those who slander you may be put to shame by your good behavior in Christ.

original.text: ⸀ἀλλὰ μετὰ πραΰτητος καὶ φόβου, συνείδησιν ἔχοντες ἀγαθήν, ἵνα ἐν ᾧ ⸀καταλαλεῖσθε καταισχυνθῶσιν οἱ ἐπηρεάζοντες ὑμῶν τὴν ἀγαθὴν ἐν Χριστῷ ἀναστροφήν.

verses.restored: For it is better, if the will of Divine should will, to suffer doing good than doing harm.

familiar.text: For it is better, if the will of God be so, that ye suffer for well doing, than for evil doing.

modern.text: For it is better, if it is God’s will, to suffer for doing good than for doing evil.

original.text: κρεῖττον γὰρ ἀγαθοποιοῦντας, εἰ θέλοι τὸ θέλημα τοῦ θεοῦ, πάσχειν ἢ κακοποιοῦντας.

verses.restored: Because Messiah also suffered once concerning sins/misalignments, righteous/just on behalf of unrighteous/unjust, so that he might bring you to the Divine, put to death in flesh but made alive in Spirit,

familiar.text: For Christ also hath once suffered for sins, the just for the unjust, that he might bring us to God, being put to death in the flesh, but quickened by the Spirit:

modern.text: For Christ also suffered for sins once for all, the righteous for the unrighteous, to bring you to God. He was put to death in the body but made alive in the Spirit,

original.text: ὅτι καὶ Χριστὸς ἅπαξ περὶ ἁμαρτιῶν ⸀ἔπαθεν, δίκαιος ὑπὲρ ἀδίκων, ἵνα ⸀ὑμᾶς προσαγάγῃ τῷ θεῷ, θανατωθεὶς μὲν σαρκὶ ζῳοποιηθεὶς δὲ πνεύματι·

verses.restored: in which also he went and proclaimed to the spirits in prison,

familiar.text: By which also he went and preached unto the spirits in prison;

modern.text: in whom He also went and preached to the spirits in prison

original.text: ἐν ᾧ καὶ τοῖς ἐν φυλακῇ πνεύμασιν πορευθεὶς ἐκήρυξεν,

verses.restored: who formerly disobeyed, when the patience of the Divine waited in days of Noah, while ark was being prepared, in which few, that is eight souls/lives, were brought safely through water.

familiar.text: Which sometime were disobedient, when once the longsuffering of God waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was a preparing, wherein few, that is, eight souls were saved by water.

modern.text: who disobeyed long ago when God waited patiently in the days of Noah while the ark was being built. In the ark a few people, only eight souls, were saved through water.

original.text: ἀπειθήσασίν ποτε ὅτε ἀπεξεδέχετο ἡ τοῦ θεοῦ μακροθυμία ἐν ἡμέραις Νῶε κατασκευαζομένης κιβωτοῦ εἰς ἣν ⸀ὀλίγοι, τοῦτʼ ἔστιν ὀκτὼ ψυχαί, διεσώθησαν διʼ ὕδατος.

verses.restored: Which also now as corresponding pattern saves/heals you: baptism, not putting away dirt of flesh, but appeal/pledge of good conscience toward Divine, through resurrection of Jesus Messiah,

familiar.text: The like figure whereunto even baptism doth also now save us (not the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but the answer of a good conscience toward God,) by the resurrection of Jesus Christ:

modern.text: And this water symbolizes the baptism that now saves you also—not the removal of dirt from the body, but the pledge of a clear conscience toward God—through the resurrection of Jesus Christ,

original.text: ὃ ⸂καὶ ὑμᾶς ἀντίτυπον νῦν⸃ σῴζει βάπτισμα, οὐ σαρκὸς ἀπόθεσις ῥύπου ἀλλὰ συνειδήσεως ἀγαθῆς ἐπερώτημα εἰς θεόν, διʼ ἀναστάσεως Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ,

verses.restored: who is at right hand of Divine, having gone into heaven, messengers and authorities and powers being arranged under him.

familiar.text: Who is gone into heaven, and is on the right hand of God; angels and authorities and powers being made subject unto him.

modern.text: who has gone into heaven and is at the right hand of God, with angels, authorities, and powers subject to Him.

original.text: ὅς ἐστιν ἐν ⸀δεξιᾷ θεοῦ πορευθεὶς εἰς οὐρανὸν ὑποταγέντων αὐτῷ ἀγγέλων καὶ ἐξουσιῶν καὶ δυνάμεων.

safety_note: 1 Peter 3:1-7 must not be used to sanctify patriarchy, coercion, or domestic abuse. The passage is held within the wider command to do good without fear, husbands honoring wives as co-heirs of grace of life, and prayers being hindered by dishonor. Reception-history audit required.
translation_notes: Apologia is defense/explanation of hope with gentleness and reverence, not combative apologetics.
Spirits in prison and baptism correspondence require second-pass audit; ambiguity is preserved.
